summary: Seek bounded message pages through body-free temporal selectors

replay.detail: Opening an older database installs selector source capture and durable progress without building the first full cut. After both APIs begin serving, the background worker backfills local message selector headers from current message projections and retained canonical claims in short, resumable chunks. Starting a backfill invalidates existing page cuts. No authoritative claim replay or body-copy inventory is introduced; ordinary pages fold only selected message bodies. Page serialization and delivery enrichment run together on a blocking worker inside the selector/body read snapshot, rather than reading the store on the async executor.

schema.detail: Adds local_client_message_selectors_v1: a body-free header/pending/quarantine table with twenty-two indexes and seven source-change triggers, completed-cut and resumable backfill/fold markers. Five retained-cut eligibility indexes contain retired headers only; historical open pages combine bounded live and retired index branches, avoiding duplicate historical-index writes on ordinary sends. The seventh trigger queues full folds/quarantine for message repairs and repaired replacement reselections. local_client_message_fold_batches stores only batch IDs/legacy wire-position prefix counts and skips scratch persistence for single-row completed prefixes. local_client_message_publications stores retention cohorts only when a retirement needs its first covering publication, plus the initial bootstrap cohort; cut advances without retirement add no cohort. Retired headers remain until their first covering publication is older than the cursor lifetime; bounded cohort cleanup preserves the latest stored cohort. The fold marker retains canonical keys and selection scalars, never content or attachments. Suspended full folds retain append progress/extend their cut; destructive epoch changes or newly dirty metadata-only bases restart them. Runtime::before_commit performs the sole selector fold at each managed outer transaction boundary, for both batched and lent writers, and composes before the source adapter finalizer. Append/apply/replay helpers no longer reset the allowance by folding eagerly. One transaction gets at most 64 claim/prefix rows and 16 subjects with a cooperative 10 ms work budget; selector/scratch cleanup is bounded. A weakly owned daemon worker drains remaining work in independent writer loans; idle checks do not borrow/commit the writer, and last-task completion wakes readers/events. Malformed desired JSON skips the subject's header, warns and increments a local counter. Desired deletion uses fixed-size indexed old/new global and recipient winner seeks rather than rewriting or inventorying an entire reminder group. A 4,096-native-member/97-declaration regression measures at most nine selector-row mutations per declaration deletion, preserves unrelated members and checks bulk owner deletion plus bounded durable draining. Final reversed-order 128-send/128-close real-append bursts measured send p95 deltas of +0.860/+0.710 ms and close p95 deltas of +0.604/+1.127 ms. Send WAL was 125,853.375 to 189,101.8125 bytes per commit (+50.26%); close WAL was 112,366.8125 to 226,374.9375 bytes per commit (+101.46%). Additional WAL per 128-commit burst was 8,095,800 bytes for sends and 14,593,040 bytes for closes. Write measurements disable automatic checkpoints to isolate WAL cost and retain production FULL synchronous commits. Page p95 ranges across limit-20 first/next filter cases were 5.044-5.772 ms at 128 messages, 5.456-6.313 ms at 1,280 and 5.772-6.815 ms at 12,800 (422,400 claims). Across five closed-heavy runs, open-page p95 ranged from 0.513 to 0.952 ms. Cursor epochs also fence repaired replacement reselections; earlier body-version tables/triggers are removed idempotently. Registry and replication compatibility digests, authoritative claims and claim formats are unchanged.

rules.detail: Canonical claim-log checkpoint rules, the schema registry digest and shared projection digests are unchanged. One background-worker guard disables automatic WAL checkpoints for the entire initial backfill lifecycle, including interleaved foreground writes; it restores the caller's policy on completion, error or unwind. The daemon WAL recycler schedules checkpoints separately. Deletion or repair that destroys a retained message cut, or a selector backfill start, invalidates that traversal instead of returning a partial successful page.

compatibility.detail: Only clients negotiating capability messages-paging version 2 with X-St3-Features: messages-paging.v2 receive the bounded paging behavior described here. Requests without that token preserve the legacy message-list shape and paging contract unchanged. Capability discovery alone does not negotiate it. Generated Rust, Swift and TypeScript clients default to legacy wire behavior and send the token only when their per-client paging option is explicitly enabled. Relays preserve negotiation only after the owner advertises messages-paging version 2; an unsupported owner never receives the new field or flag. Message JSON, recipient/actor filters, ordering, reminder selection and snapshot-consistent traversal are preserved. Bounded pages retain local body references and byte counts without inlining long text. Successful negotiated message-list responses enforce the advertised 1,048,576-byte encoded envelope ceiling; byte-truncated pages continue after the last returned item, and an oversized single resource or relayed envelope returns response-too-large instead of dropping resources. Pending selector tasks are invisible; ordinary incomplete maintenance serves and pins the last fully published frontier. Admitted remote declarations cannot advance that frontier until the durable graph projection covers them, including same-index incremental projection. Interrupted startup backfill retains its resume state and exposes no initial page cut until projection and bounded backfill complete. Desired-projection deletion immediately clears declaration-derived fields and eligibility, expires existing cursors and appears on fresh pages before reconciliation completes; retained intent.desired claims do not restore deleted fields. Its synchronous selector mutations are confined to the affected subject and old/new global and recipient winners; indexed LIMIT 1 seeks preserve canonical winner ordering and unrelated reminder-group members. Native reminder metadata and a preexisting pending row's old recipient survive deletion. Destructive claim update/delete, message repair and repaired replacement reselection expire old cursors and insert one durable born_index=-2 quarantine marker per subject; fresh pages temporarily omit that subject until replacement reconciles and its cut is published. Repaired actual claims no longer contribute routing or eligibility scalars, matching the canonical message-body fold. The desired-projection shortcut checks both later declarations and durable projection coverage; canonical fallback also excludes durably repaired originals after receipt trimming. Selector maintenance reacts to source-writer notifications, parks without idle polling, and uses independently bounded background writer loans. Continuations bind exact store cut, snapshot, filters, limit, position and expiry. Tampered, expired, evicted, restarted or deletion-invalidated cursors return HTTP 410/page-cursor-expired. Delivery presence remains live on each page while delivery age retains the first request time.

downtime.detail: The daemon does not wait for the first selector cut before serving. Initial population begins only after both APIs serve, in resumable clear, subject-queue and claim-row-bounded pending phases. Negotiated v2 message pages return HTTP 503 message-selectors-not-ready until the first complete cut is published; legacy message readers and unrelated endpoints remain available. Empty stores publish an empty cut immediately. Each online chunk uses a separate background writer loan with at most 16 subjects, 64 claim/prefix rows, 64 cleanup rows and a cooperative 10 ms fold allowance; durable COMMIT latency is not a proven hard bound. Explicit benchmark rebuilds additionally run a PASSIVE checkpoint outside chunk transactions. Earlier synchronous-open measurements do not establish the cost of this online design; final-head WAL growth and transaction durations, including legacy callers, require hosted or separately admitted measurement.

manual.detail: No manual migration, identity change or claim-log maintenance is required. Clients restart pagination on page-cursor-expired. Empty-source projection skips require an exact healthy frontier and no pending verdicts; ahead frontiers still run canonical recovery. Since commit 5e1b8c2a, a deferred replication-projection commit skips the runtime before_commit finalizer, not merely inline selector maintenance. Source maintenance and source-adapter finalizers still run atomically with that commit.

recovery.detail: Readers can briefly observe committed source ahead of runtime-derived output after a deferred replication-projection commit skips the runtime finalizer. Durable delta/pending rows remain committed with the source and recover the derived output when subsequent runtime finalization or reactive maintenance consumes them; the deferred commit is not a synchronous derived-output publication guarantee. The selector worker remembers pending work across its parked turns, so it still notifies readers when an ordinary source or tail-verdict finalizer drains that work before its next loan. Binary swap-back cannot restore issued in-memory cursor metadata; clients restart traversals. The authoritative claim log remains intact and older claim-based readers continue to work. A runtime that reintroduces the removed local body version store must recreate and seed it from claims.
